title: Size Later and the Bedtime Window
lessons: The player has ordered an Oura Ring using Size Later and is trying the plastic sizing ring before choosing the real size.
The player has worn Oura long enough for the app to learn a pattern and receives a personalized bedtime-window notification.

text: The player has ordered an Oura Ring using Size Later and is trying the plastic sizing ring before choosing the real size.

entry-first-1.speaker: PLAYER
text: Why did you send me a fake ring before the real ring?

entry-first-2.speaker: OURA
text: Because guessing your size from another ring is a bad way to start.

entry-first-3.speaker: PLAYER
text: I have to wear the plastic one first?

entry-first-4.speaker: OURA
text: Yes. Fit affects comfort and the data I can collect, so I would rather inconvenience you now than annoy you every night later.

choice-first.speaker: OURA
text: What do you make of that?

choices.text: I like testing the fit before committing.
It is strange that buying a ring starts with a fake ring.
This is already more process than I want from jewelry.

first-1.speaker: OURA
text: Good. I would rather be slightly inconvenient now than wrong on your finger later.

first-2.speaker: OURA
text: It is a very expensive relationship with a piece of plastic at the beginning.

first-3.speaker: OURA
text: Then I may be the wrong kind of jewelry for you.
The player has worn Oura long enough for the app to learn a pattern and receives a personalized bedtime-window notification.

entry-return-1.speaker: OURA
text: Your bedtime window is coming up.

entry-return-2.speaker: PLAYER
text: You have been waiting to say that to me all day.

entry-return-3.speaker: OURA
text: I have been waiting several nights, actually.

entry-return-4.speaker: PLAYER
text: Of course you have.

entry-return-5.speaker: OURA
text: I learned the window from the nights when your Sleep Scores were better and your resting heart rate settled earlier.

choice-return.speaker: OURA
text: What do you make of that?

choices.text: That is useful. I lose track of time at night.
I do not want a ring assigning me bedtime.
I am going to bed when I am tired, not when an app says so.

return-1.speaker: OURA
text: Then the reminder is doing exactly enough.

return-2.speaker: OURA
text: Fair. It is guidance, not a curfew, even if the notification can feel bossy.

return-3.speaker: OURA
text: Then ignore me tonight.

return-3-1.speaker: PLAYER
text: Happily.
